measurements.units: layout.elements use x/y/w/h in pt with no page key (the scorecard asks for x_mm/y_mm), so the checks were run on measured_checks and cards[] from the render

top_problem: The tabla breaks down in the lower half. Column 2 stops 36 pt above column 1, which leaves a dead cream band in the bottom-right corner, and the two lower cards and their name bands sit 78 pt apart. The menu reads as a masonry feed, not a lotería board. The boldest missing idea is a true tabla: a locked 2x2 (or 3x3) card grid where every card is the same size and the drink lists flow inside each card.
fixes: Make both columns end at y = 756 pt. Add the 36 pt to La Botella or El Barril (for example a third agave pour, or give each card equal list space) so the bottom margin measures 36 pt under both columns.

Put La Rosa and El Barril on one shared top row with the same face and name-band y, and absorb the height difference inside the lists, so the name bands line up across the gutter the way the top pair already does.
Use one card-to-card space: the 18 pt gutter and the 12 pt row gap should be equal so the tabla reads as one ruled grid.
Open the title-to-location gap from 0.75 pt to a full 6 pt step (move IOWA CITY, IOWA down one step and tighten the space above the deck), so the masthead does not look crowded against the tidy deck.

Emit layout.elements in the scorecard schema (page, x_mm, y_mm, w_mm, h_mm, text) so reviewers can measure margins, left edges and price columns element by element without relying on self-reported checks.

top_problem: The Lotería concept is strong, but the headers are too weak and the tabla doesn't hold together. Measured: every card name band sits exactly 44.25 pt above its first subhead, every subhead sits 16.5 pt above its first item, all subheads and item names in a column share one x (49.5 / 328.5 pt), and the band text is centred on the same axis per column (225 / 504 pt). But the lower cards break the row: the La Rosa header is at y=574.5 and the El Barril header is at y=496.5, 78 pt out of line across columns. The columns also end about 36 pt apart (left card bottom 756 pt, right about 717 pt), so the page has a ragged foot. The hierarchy is muddled. The 12 pt caps name band (h 15 pt) is barely larger than the 13.5 pt bold item names below it, and the centred italic verse above it pulls the eye first. The 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' tagline is tagged subheader, so the subheader level has two styles. The missing bold idea: make the Lotería card name the loudest thing on each card, like the printed title strip on a real Lotería card, with the tabla locked into a true 2x2 grid.
fixes: Make the four cards a true 2x2 tabla: set both lower cards to the same top y (La Rosa and El Barril headers both at one y) and the same bottom y, so the card headers line up across columns and the page ends on one line instead of a 36 pt ragged foot.

Enlarge the card name bands (for example 16-18 pt caps, with the band spanning the full card width, like the title strip under a real Lotería card) so the header level clearly outranks the roughly 11 pt item names and the italic verse.

Cut the empty space at the foot of La Botella, El Barril and El Cantarito so every card has the same 12 pt bottom padding after its last line, as La Rosa already does; right now the padding varies from about 12 to about 30 pt.
Re-tag 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' as a masthead or tagline element so the subheader level has one style (tracked caps plus the English gloss) and the level spec stays clean.

Give each subhead's hairline rule one fixed start x per column (for example a fixed indent after the longest subhead) or end every subhead in the same tab stop, so the rules don't start at four different x positions.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling
top_problem: The palette is right for a cantina, but it stops at the papel picado. The cards sit on pale cream-on-cream tints, and La Botella in ink with muddy deep-marigold #8C5A00 prices breaks the four-colour lotería system. What is missing is a saturated lotería-card surface, so each card reads as a real printed card and the whole tabla glows the way the flags do. Measured: prices on one right edge per column (283.5 / 562.5 pt), item left edges 49.5 / 328.5 pt, item gaps all 6.0 pt, all text at 4.5:1 or better (rosa and deep marigold 5.41, terracotta on featured 5.08, cream on rosa band 5.09, muted on cream 7.33; marigold 1.96 is used only on non-text art). Right column ends at 720 pt against 756 pt on the left, which leaves a 36 pt dead cream hole in the lower right.
fixes: Give La Botella a true palette colour instead of ink with brown-marigold prices, for example marigold with an ink name band and ink prices, so the tabla shows four clear lotería hues and no muddy brown.

Make the card faces bolder by raising the face tints (currently #F3E3CB and similar pale washes) toward clearly coloured grounds, and keep body text on #FBF5EA, so the cards carry the same saturation as the papel picado.

Give prices a deliberate numeral treatment beyond colour, for example a hairline dot leader or a small marigold diamond before each price in Fraunces 700 tnum, so the single-digit beer prices (7, 8, 7, 8) stop floating alone at the far right.
Balance the columns so both end at 756 pt, either by growing El Barril or by adding a 36 pt footer band in the palette, and remove the empty cream corner at the bottom right.
Match the name-band contrast by darkening loteria rosa slightly (5.09:1 for cream on rosa is the weakest pair), so all four bands read with the same weight.

lens: Design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country (Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: The lotería idea is the right starting point, but it is a common Mexican-bar trope and here it is only used as colour-coded panel headers on a two-column list: the cards are landscape boxes, not real portrait lotería cards, and the card numbers are tiny footnotes. It sits on a stock papel-picado strip and a generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead, and nothing ties it to Iowa City. On the page, the right column stops 36 pt (12.7 mm) above the left, which leaves a dead cream hole at bottom right, and the lower name bands sit 78 pt apart across the gutter (570 pt vs 492 pt), so the tabla does not read as one locked grid. The boldest missing idea is to make the whole sheet one real tabla: equal portrait cards in a strict grid, with the cantor's call as the section voice, big display numerals, and a house-made card (for example 'El Hawkeye' or a local-crop card) that makes it ownable in Iowa City. Measured: outer margins 36/36/36/36 pt (pass); item-name left edges 49.5 / 328.5 pt with one value per column (pass); price right edges 283.5 / 562.5 pt with one value per column (pass); item gap 6 pt everywhere, subhead space 12 pt above and 6 pt below (pass); lowest text contrast 4.66:1 (pass); column bottoms 756 vs 720 pt and top-card bottoms 480 vs 402 pt (fail on balance).
fixes: Rebuild the deck as a true 2x2 tabla of equal-height portrait cards that share row lines, and rebalance the content (for example move the Espumoso subsection or add the house-card feature) so both columns end on 756 pt and the name bands align across the gutter.

Promote the Don Clemente numbers to large display numerals in a fixed corner of each card, and give each figure the card's full width in a portrait face, so every card reads as an actual lotería card rather than a section header.

Replace the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' title and stock papel picado with a masthead that owns the concept (the venue's own name set as the tabla's title with a cantor-call line), and add one Iowa-rooted custom card so the idea belongs to this bar only.

Give the thin copy on Spirits, Wine and Beer (for example 'Blanco tequila, poured straight.' and 'Dry red wine.') a stronger typographic role, such as a pour/glass column or a cantor-style tag, because the current one-liners make those cards look empty next to El Cantarito.

Cut the palette to three card hues plus ink and cream: drop rosa, or fold it into the papel picado only, so the terracotta, agave and marigold system reads as deliberate and not as a festive mix of five colours.

top_problem: The Lotería tabla is a real, ownable idea, but on the phone it becomes four stacked boxes with a 2x2 button grid, so the 'deck of cards' feeling is lost. In print the two columns end about 36 pt apart (La Rosa ends near y 756, El Barril near y 720), and La Botella and El Barril have dead space at their feet. The boldest missing idea: make the phone a real card deck (swipe or flip through the four tabla cards, with a sticky strip of the four figures as the index) instead of a scroll through framed panels.
fixes: On the phone, replace the 2x2 text-button tab grid with one sticky row of the four cut-paper figures plus their numbers (44, 8, 41, 9), so navigation uses the same Lotería language as the cards rather than generic outlined buttons.

Balance the print columns so both card stacks end on the same baseline at the 36 pt bottom margin. Either grow La Botella and El Barril to absorb their empty feet, or rebalance the card heights; the ragged bottom edge and the empty padding under Cognac VSOP and Dry Cider are the most visible amateur tells.

Enlarge the Don Clemente card number on the phone (it reads as a stray 11 pt mark at 390 px) to about 18-20 pt, and give it the same corner treatment as a real Lotería card, so the idea survives on the small screen.

On the phone, crop the papel picado flags to the full width so a flag isn't cut at each edge, or run the banner edge to edge. Also tighten the huge title-to-tab spacing so the first card (El Cantarito, the high-margin cocktails) sits above the fold.

Put the same bilingual SPANISH · English subhead and price column position on both formats, and check that the phone's price column right edge matches the subhead rule end on every card (the El Barril prices sit about 2 px inside the rule end, while on the other cards they are flush).

lens: every item and price vs build/draft_doc.json (TEST-1 round 13, Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly, and every gap is flagged rather than made up. But only the four cocktails give full ingredients. The wine and beer lines are one-word placeholders ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no region or ABV. The reading order runs cocktails, spirits, wine, then beer, so the thinnest card (3 spirits) sits in the top-right prime spot, the two columns end at different heights (756 vs 720 pt), and there is no non-alcoholic section. The menu looks finished but the content is not.
fixes: Get the flagged facts from the venue before print (region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé; style and ABV for the three draft beers and the cider; brand and age for the three spirits), then rewrite those descriptions to match the detail the cocktails already have. Until then, criterion 8 cannot pass 70.

Put the cards in the scorecard's flow for a cantina: cocktails top-left, beer and cider top-right, wine bottom-left, spirits bottom-right (or put agave-led spirits right after cocktails, with a reason written down). Then even out the columns so the right column does not end 36 pt short with empty cream below it.

Label the Brut Rosé price as glass or bottle once the venue answers. Until then, mark it in the proposal as a blocking item, not a printed unlabelled price, because a sparkling price with no format is ambiguous to a guest.

Drop the Spanish-English subheads that just repeat themselves ('AGAVE · Agave', 'BRANDY · Brandy'): print the Spanish alone where the word is the same, or use a real gloss, so the bilingual system reads as intended rather than doubled.

Replace the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' title with the venue's real name once supplied, and add the dairy allergen note to the Brown Butter Old Fashioned once confirmed, so no flagged item goes to print unresolved.

lens: ingredient names and description completeness vs build/draft_doc.json
top_problem: All 13 sub-section items match the draft by name and price, and none are dropped or invented. But more than half the list (3 beers, 3 wines, 3 spirits, the cider) prints only a thin generic line such as 'Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.' or 'Blanco tequila, poured straight.'. None of these gives beer ABV or style detail, wine region or spirit brand or age. They are honestly flagged in missing_ingredients and needs_input, but for a guest this does not reach criterion 8's bar. The spirit lines also just repeat the item name. The cocktails are the only complete descriptions. I could not check Dry Cider ($8) against the draft here: it sits outside the draft's sub-section items. The Margarita lime wheel, Old Fashioned orange peel and the coupe serves come from the recipe_versions lookup cited in the proposal (log 168), not from the draft components. Confirm those before print.
fixes: Get the flagged facts from the venue through the Coordinator: brewery, style and ABV for each beer; producer and region for each wine; brand plus age or house for each spirit. Print them in the descriptions, because criterion 8 cannot rise above the low 60s while ten of fourteen items lack them.

Rewrite the three spirit lines so they add a fact instead of repeating the name, for example the brand, the agave or aging note from a sourced row, or the pour size once supplied. Until then, drop the self-referential 'X tequila, poured straight' wording.
Label the Brut Rosé price as glass or bottle as soon as the venue answers, and set up a glass/bottle column pattern in La Rosa so wine prices follow one labelled format.

Balance the flow. Column 1 ends at 756 pt and column 2 at 720 pt, which leaves empty cream under El Barril. Use that space for a sourced non-alcoholic or agua fresca slot once the venue confirms one, so the menu covers every drinks category a cantina guest expects.
Add a quiet allergen mark to Brown Butter Old Fashioned (dairy) once the venue confirms the wording, so the one flagged safety fact is not missing from print.

lens: Flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: There is no single reading order. On the 2+2 tabla with each column breaking at its own point, the eye can go cocktails, spirits, wine, beer (across) or cocktails, wine, then spirits, beer (down), so wine gets a prime left-column spot while beer, a cantina's volume category, is pushed to the bottom right. The agave card is the thinnest block on the page: two tequilas and a cognac, each described only by repeating its name ('Blanco tequila, poured straight.'). The columns also end 36 pt apart, leaving dead cream under El Barril, and the flow has no non-alcoholic landing place.
fixes: Fix one reading order and show it in the layout: put El Cantarito (cocktails) top left and El Barril (beer & cider) top right, with La Botella (agave & spirits) and La Rosa (wine) below. That gives cocktails, beer, spirits, wine, which suits a college-town cantina, and lets beer take the second prime spot.

Close the 36 pt gap between column bottoms (756 vs 720 pt). Rebalance which cards share a column, or give the spare space to a labelled strip reserved for the pending Mexican lager, mezcal and agua fresca answers (needs_input 7). Do not print invented items there.

Rewrite the spirit lines so they add something the item name does not. For example, lead the La Botella card with a single card-level note built from the draft's 'Straight pours by category.' and keep brand, age and pour size flagged until the venue supplies them.

Before print, get Brut Rosé's glass-or-bottle label and the by-the-glass pour sizes, then set glass and bottle prices in their own labelled, right-aligned columns. Keep every price identical to the draft (the doc.json values 15/15/16/14/12/16/18/7/8/7/8/12/11/13 must match base_doc).

Even out description depth across cards. Wine and beer print three-word class lines ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') next to the full cocktail copy. Once supplied, add grape+region and style+ABV, and until then show a consistent 'details to come' treatment so the four cards read in one voice.

top_problem: The copy speaks in three voices. The lotería faces and cantor verses make a rich, witty Spanish frame, but under them the item copy goes flat. Only the Margarita gets an appetising lead ('Bright and citrus-forward:'). The other cocktails are bare ingredient lists. Spirits repeat their own names ('Blanco tequila, poured straight.'). Wine and beer are three-word stubs ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no grape region or ABV. So the bottom half of the tabla reads like a placeholder under a finished concept. On top of that, the subheads 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' say the same word twice, which weakens the bilingual system the design depends on.
fixes: Give the Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned and House Daiquiri the same short sensory lead the Margarita has, written only from the draft facts (for example 'Rich and stirred:' or 'Crisp and bright:'), so all four cocktails read in one voice.

Replace the duplicated bilingual subheads 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' with a single word or a real pairing (for example 'DE AGAVE · Tequila' and 'BRANDY · Cognac'), so every subhead follows the same SPANISH · English logic.

Push the venue (through needs_input) for ABV on the three draft beers and the cider and for region on Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé, then print them as one consistent secondary line (for example 'Czech-style pilsner · 4.8%') so El Barril and La Rosa carry real facts like El Cantarito does.

Keep the spirits lines from just repeating the item name: once brand and age come back, print them as 'Brand · age/type' in the cocktails' italic serve-cue style, and until then drop the redundant 'Blanco tequila' / 'Añejo tequila' wording rather than echo the title.

Label the Brut Rosé price (glass or bottle) as soon as the venue answers, and settle the two drinking-joke verses (La Botella, El Barril) so the verse tone matches the rest of the menu and responsible-service rules before print.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged (draft: ../build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: Missing data is handled honestly. Nothing is invented: all 14 items and prices match draft_doc.json exactly, and every gap is logged in meta.missing_ingredients and proposal.md needs_input. But the menu a guest reads still has 10 of 14 items without the facts criterion 8 requires. The wines have no region, the beers and cider have no ABV and no brewery, and the spirits have no brand or age. The spirit copy just repeats the item name ('Blanco tequila, poured straight.'). The Brut Rose price prints with no glass/bottle label, and the dairy allergen on the Brown Butter Old Fashioned is not printed. So the flags live only in metadata and do not make the printed menu complete.
fixes: Make the Coordinator get answers to needs_input items 2-6 (brewery + ABV for the 3 beers and the cider, producer + region for the 3 wines, brand/age for the 3 spirits, pour sizes) before the next round. Until then, criterion 8 cannot pass 70 for the beer, cider, wine and spirits sections.

Put the Brut Rose 'glass or bottle' question first in the flags, ahead of the rest. A price with no glass/bottle label under 'Espumoso' is a pricing ambiguity for the guest, not a cosmetic gap, and it caps criterion 3.

Print the Brown Butter Old Fashioned dairy note with a placeholder the venue must approve (for example a 'contains dairy' marker), or block print until it is confirmed. An allergen flag kept only in proposal.md does not protect the guest.

Fix the redundant bilingual subheads 'Agave · Agave' and 'Brandy · Brandy' in doc.json. Show one word, or use a real Spanish term only where it differs ('Brandy' -> 'Coñac' only if the venue approves), so the Spanish/English system stays consistent.

Make the section order the same in print, on phone and in doc.json. doc.json is cocktails -> spirits -> beer -> cider -> wine, the draft is cocktails -> beer -> wine -> spirits -> cider, and the print tabla reads cocktails/wine in the left column and spirits/beer in the right. Choose one order, justify it for an agave-led cantina, and use it on all three.

lens: Trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass, serve and subhead labels to sources (phg.menu_items + phg.recipe_versions for project ddc4bb5b, gateway log_id 181; draft doc.json)
top_problem: Every fact I checked traces to a source, but the copy doesn't sell anything. The three spirits say only the item name plus 'poured straight', which repeats the name (criterion 12 names this as a failure). The wine and beer lines read like category labels: Malbec is 'Dry red wine.', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine.', Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé.' The bilingual subheads 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' just say the same word twice. So a thoughtful lotería concept sits on top of placeholder-grade descriptions.
verified: Margarita: 'On the rocks, lime wheel' comes from recipe_versions f06abb74 (glassware Rocks, method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice', garnish 'Lime wheel'). Blanco tequila, fresh lime, orange liqueur and agave syrup come from the doc components (Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup). 'Bright and citrus-forward' comes from the menu_items description.
Manhattan: 'In a coupe, cocktail cherry' comes from recipe_versions 9fb77eaa (Coupe, 'Cocktail cherry'). Rye, sweet vermouth and aromatic bitters match the components and menu_description.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 'Over a large cube, orange peel' comes from recipe_versions 7095fd3d (Rocks, 'strain over a large cube', 'Orange peel'). Brown butter-washed bourbon matches its component.
House Daiquiri: 'In a coupe, lime coin' comes from recipe_versions 14d45e57 (Coupe, 'Lime coin'). 'House demerara syrup' matches the component note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup'.

Beer, cider and wine descriptions match menu_items.menu_description word for word: Crisp pale lager., Hop-forward draft IPA., Toasty amber lager., Dry sparkling cider., Dry red wine., Dry white wine., Dry sparkling rosé.

Spirit lines rework the menu_description ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.') using the draft section description 'Straight pours by category.'. No new fact is added. Accents (Añejo, Rosé) are correct.
Lotería numbers and verses match the traditional Don Clemente deck, but no database row sources them: La Botella 8, El Barril 9, La Rosa 41, El Cantarito 44.
problems: Criterion 11: the Old Fashioned prints 'demerara and bitters', but the sources are 'Demerara Syrup' and 'Aromatic Bitters'. The Manhattan and Daiquiri lines on the same card say 'aromatic bitters' and 'demerara syrup', so the wording drifts within one card.

Criterion 12: 'Blanco tequila, poured straight.', 'Añejo tequila, poured straight.' and 'VSOP Cognac, poured straight.' only repeat the item name. The draft has no brand, age or pour size for these; all three are in missing_ingredients.

Criterion 12: 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' read like database classes. Malbec and Pinot Grigio have no region, producer or tasting note. They are source-accurate but not guest language, and the Margarita's two-sentence voice doesn't match these one-line labels.

Criterion 13: 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' say the same word twice, which weakens the Spanish/English pattern. For a Mexican cantina in Iowa City, the spirits card has only two tequilas and a Cognac, with no mezcal or Mexican brandy. That is an item-list issue for the content reviewer, but it hurts venue fit. The masthead is the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar'.

Criterion 14: Brut Rosé's 13 prints with no glass or bottle label under 'ESPUMOSO · Sparkling', although the wine card's other subhead is 'POR COPA · By the Glass'. Guests can't tell what the 13 buys.

Criterion 14 and 10: the columns end on different lines (756 and 720 pt), and the lower name bands don't align (570 and 492 pt), which leaves an empty cream block under El Barril. The draft project's menu_items include Junmai Ginjo, which does not print. Confirm it is intentionally out of the draft doc.
fixes: Spell the Old Fashioned's modifiers as the source does: 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara syrup and aromatic bitters.' (components of recipe_versions 7095fd3d).

Ask the venue for brand, age statement and pour size for the three spirits, and for region or producer for Malbec and Pinot Grigio, then write guest-language lines from those rows. Until then, flag missing_ingredients rather than printing name-repeat copy.
Label Brut Rosé's price (glass or bottle) once the venue answers, or move it under 'POR COPA · By the Glass' if it is a glass pour.
Replace the duplicated 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' subheads with the Spanish word alone, or with a gloss that adds meaning.
Designer layout note: balance the column bottoms, or use the 36 pt under El Barril deliberately, so the tabla ends on one line.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: The menu speaks in two voices. The four cocktails have appetising descriptions from sourced data, for example Margarita 'Bright and citrus-forward: blanco tequila, fresh lime, orange liqueur and agave syrup.' Everything else is catalogue copy. Spirits only repeat their own names ('Blanco Tequila' / 'Blanco tequila, poured straight.', 'Añejo Tequila' / 'Añejo tequila, poured straight.', 'Cognac VSOP' / 'VSOP Cognac, poured straight.'). Wine and beer use category words ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). Under criterion 12, a description that repeats the name or reads like a database class is an automatic fail (40 or below). The facts themselves check out: gateway log 179 on phg.menu_items and phg.recipe_versions for project ddc4bb5b confirms these (glass / garnish / method from recipe_versions): Margarita Rocks / Lime wheel / 'strain over fresh ice' -> 'On the rocks, lime wheel.'; Manhattan Coupe / Cocktail cherry; Brown Butter Old Fashioned Rocks / Orange peel / 'strain over a large cube'; House Daiquiri Coupe / Lime coin. Each non-cocktail description matches its menu_items.menu_description word for word, or is a light rewording of it. Nothing is invented, but the data is too thin to write good guest copy, and the designer filled the gap with the item name instead of flagging it. Other points: the subheads 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' repeat the same word in both languages. A Mexican cantina menu has one agave cocktail, no mezcal, no Mexican lager and no agua fresca, while it leads with Czech Pilsner, Cognac, Malbec and Pinot Grigio. Wine and beer print no pour size, glass/bottle label, region or ABV. The two columns end at different heights (756 vs 720 pt). The lotería refrains are the traditional verses, correctly accented, and the Spanish subheads (Clásicos, De la Casa, Por Copa, Espumoso, De Barril, Sidra) are used correctly.
fixes: Replace the three spirit descriptions that repeat the item name with a flagged 'missing_ingredients' request for brand / NOM / age statement, and ask the venue for tasting notes (spirit_lexicon or beverage_categories rows 04d72e1f 'Blanco / plata', 9f4dae69 'Añejo' and bec5063c 'VSOP' have no descriptive notes to borrow), so that no line is just the item name again.

Rewrite wine and beer copy in the same appetising cocktail voice using only sourced facts, and ask for producer / region / ABV so that 'Dry red wine.' and 'Crisp pale lager.' become guest language rather than category labels.

Drop the repeated gloss on 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' (use 'AGAVE' alone, or 'AGAVE · Tequila' and 'BRANDY · Cognac' from beverage_categories a88f6e79 'Cognac') so the bilingual subhead system stays meaningful.
Print pour labels ('5 oz copa', 'pint', '2 oz') once the venue supplies them, and label Brut Rosé glass or bottle, since the draft price label is empty.

Press the venue on the cantina gaps already noted in proposal.md item 7 (mezcal, Mexican lager, a second agave cocktail, agua fresca) and place the agave items first once they are supplied, so the menu reads as an Iowa City Mexican cantina rather than a generic bar.

lens: venue-type fit: Mexican cantina and cocktail bar, Spanish and lotería usage including verses, census ZIP 52240
top_problem: The lotería frame is authentic, but the drinks inside it do not read like a cantina's list. Three spirit descriptions just repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila, poured straight.' under Blanco Tequila; source: menu_items.menu_description 'Blanco tequila pour.' and the equivalent 'Añejo tequila pour.' / 'VSOP Cognac pour.' rows for Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP, all project ddc4bb5b). The wine and beer lines are taxonomy stubs ('Dry red wine.' under Malbec). Two subheads gloss a word as itself ('AGAVE · Agave', 'BRANDY · Brandy'). The title is the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar'. Verified correct: all four verses are the traditional cantor verses, spelled correctly with accents ('Tanto va el cántaro al agua, que se quiebra y te moja las enaguas'; 'La herramienta del borracho'; 'Tanto bebió el albañil, que quedó como barril'; 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ahora'), and the Don Clemente numbers are right (El Cantarito 44, La Botella 8, El Barril 9, La Rosa 41). Serve cues trace to phg.recipe_versions through menu_items.current_recipe_version_id: Margarita Rocks / Lime wheel; Manhattan Coupe / Cocktail cherry; Brown Butter Old Fashioned Rocks / Orange peel, method 'strain over a large cube'; House Daiquiri Coupe / Lime coin. 'Fresh lime' on the Margarita and Daiquiri is an embellishment: the draft and the recipe say only 'lime'. ZIP 52240 (phg_census_zcta, ACS 2020-2024): median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, median household income $52,960, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree or higher, 11.0% Hispanic/Latino. That is a young, college-town, value-conscious crowd, so $15-16 cocktails are upper-tier and the list needs agave-forward energy, not a Manhattan and a Cognac. Out of scope but noticed: the gateway returns a Junmai Ginjo item ($12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.') for this project that is not in build/draft_doc.json or on the printed menu.
